docs.title: Design System Spec
docs.text: A declarative, machine-readable specification for defining complete design systems as code.

docs.title: What is DSS?
docs.text: Design System Spec (DSS) provides a canonical framework for expressing design systems (like Material Design, Carbon, Fluent) in a structured, version-controlled, LLM-optimized format.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Declarative definitions - Define tokens, components, patterns as data
  • Multi-format support - JSON/YAML for tokens, Markdown for documentation
  • LLM optimization - Explicit intent, contexts, and constraints for AI code generation
  • Code generation - Generate CSS, TypeScript types, and LLM prompts from spec
  • Theming contracts - Formal theming API between component libraries and applications
  • Diagram generation - Mermaid and D2 diagrams for architecture visualization
  • Compliance validation - Validate implementations against the spec
  • Go-first approach - Go structs as source of truth, generating JSON Schema

docs.title: Quick Install
docs.text:
# Install CLI
go install github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/cmd/dss@latest

# Install Go SDK
go get github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/sdk/go

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
# Show design system info
dss info

# Generate CSS, TypeScript types, and LLM context
dss generate --css ./src/index.css --types ./src/lib/types.ts --llm ./DESIGN_CONTEXT.md

# Generate theme bindings for external components
dss bind --output ./theme.css

# Validate theming contracts
dss contract validate

# Validate component implementations
dss validate ./src/components

docs.title: Canonical Layers
docs.text:
DSS defines 10 canonical layers for complete design system specification:

Layer Purpose Meta System metadata (name, version, maintainers) Principles Design philosophy and guidelines Foundations Design tokens (colors, typography, spacing) Components UI elements with variants and states Patterns Multi-component solutions Templates Page layouts Content Voice & tone guidelines Accessibility WCAG compliance requirements Governance Versioning and deprecation policies Theming Token mappings to external components

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The dss command-line tool generates code artifacts and validates implementations against design system specifications.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go install github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/cmd/dss@latest

docs.title: Global Flags

docs.title: dss info
docs.text:
Display information about a design system specification.

dss info [flags]

Examples:

# Show info for current directory
dss info

# Show info for a specific directory
dss info -d ./my-design-system

Output includes:

  • Design system name and version
  • Description
  • Principles count
  • Foundation token counts (colors, typography, spacing)
  • Component list with variant counts
  • Accessibility target level
  • Validation status

docs.title: dss generate
docs.text:
Generate code artifacts from a design system specification.

dss generate [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description --css Output path for CSS file --types Output path for TypeScript types --llm Output path for LLM prompt/context --css-format CSS format: tailwind4 (default), css-vars, scss

Examples:

# Preview all outputs to stdout
dss generate

# Generate CSS only
dss generate --css ./src/index.css

# Generate all artifacts
dss generate \
  --css ./src/index.css \
  --types ./src/lib/design-system-types.ts \
  --llm ./DESIGN_CONTEXT.md

# Use different spec directory
dss generate -d ./design-system --css ./web/src/styles.css

# Generate SCSS variables instead of Tailwind
dss generate --css-format scss --css ./src/variables.scss

# Generate standard CSS custom properties
dss generate --css-format css-vars --css ./src/vars.css

# Generate NPM package with all targets
dss generate --package ./dist --targets all

# Generate NPM package with specific targets
dss generate --package ./dist --targets css,tailwind,shadcn

NPM Package Flags:

Flag Short Description --package -p Output directory for NPM package --scope -s NPM scope (e.g., @myorg) --name -n Package name (default: design-tokens) --targets -t Comma-separated targets (default: css,tailwind) --dry-run Preview without writing files

Available Targets:

Target Description css CSS custom properties tailwind Tailwind CSS v4 preset shadcn ShadCN/UI theme variables mkdocs-material MkDocs Material theme scss SCSS variables json Raw JSON tokens w3c W3C Design Tokens format all All of the above

Generated Package Exports:

The generated package.json includes these exports for consumers:

Export Path File Usage . index.mjs / index.js import { colors } from '@myorg/design-tokens' ./css css/tokens.css @import '@myorg/design-tokens/css' ./tailwind tailwind/preset.js import preset from '@myorg/design-tokens/tailwind' ./shadcn shadcn/theme.css @import '@myorg/design-tokens/shadcn' ./mkdocs mkdocs/extra.css extra_css: ['.../@myorg/design-tokens/mkdocs'] ./scss scss/_variables.scss @import '@myorg/design-tokens/scss'

See NPM Package Spec for full package.json structure.

CSS Formats:

Format Description tailwind4 Tailwind CSS v4 @theme block with CSS custom properties css-vars Standard CSS :root with custom properties scss SCSS variables ($color-primary, etc.)

docs.title: dss validate
docs.text:
Validate that component implementations comply with the design system specification.

dss validate <components-dir> [flags]

Arguments:

Argument Description components-dir Directory containing React/TypeScript component files

Flags:

Flag Description --json Output results as JSON (useful for CI)

Examples:

# Validate components
dss validate ./src/components

# Validate with different spec directory
dss validate -d ./design-system ./web/src/components

# JSON output for CI integration
dss validate --json ./src/components

Validation Checks:

Rule Severity Description no-hardcoded-colors Warning Hex/RGB/HSL colors should use CSS variables use-spacing-scale Warning Pixel values should use spacing scale img-alt-required Error Images must have alt attributes button-accessible-name Warning Icon-only buttons need aria-label valid-variant Error Variant values must match component spec single-primary-button Warning Only one primary button per view no-nested-cards Warning Cards should not be nested

Exit Codes:

Code Meaning 0 Validation passed (may have warnings) 1 Validation failed with errors

docs.title: dss bind
docs.text:
Generate theme bindings from design system token mappings.

dss bind [flags]

Flags:

Flag Short Description --output -o Output file (default: stdout) --format -f Output format: css, typescript, scss (default: css) --strategy Mapping strategy: explicit, semantic, inherit (default: explicit)

Examples:

# Generate CSS bindings to stdout
dss bind

# Generate CSS to file
dss bind --output ./theme.css

# Generate TypeScript constants
dss bind --format typescript --output ./theme.ts

# Use semantic auto-mapping
dss bind --strategy semantic --output ./theme.css

# Generate SCSS variables
dss bind --format scss --output ./theme.scss

Mapping Strategies:

Strategy Description explicit Only use defined from/to mappings, skip unmapped tokens semantic Auto-map by semantic field, fall back to component defaults inherit Use component defaults for all unmapped tokens

docs.title: dss contract validate
docs.text:
Validate all theming contracts in the design system.

dss contract validate [flags]

Flags:

Flag Description --json Output as JSON instead of table

Examples:

# Validate all contracts
dss contract validate

# JSON output for CI
dss contract validate --json

Validation Checks:

Check Severity Description Prefix required Error Contract must have a prefix starting with -- Token ID required Error Each token must have a unique ID CSS property required Error Each token must have a cssProperty Duplicate token ID Error Token IDs must be unique within a contract CSS property prefix Warning cssProperty should start with the contract prefix Invalid semantic Warning Semantic value should be from the allowed set Missing defaults Warning Tokens should have defaultLight and defaultDark

Output:

✓ button: OK
⚠ card: 2 warnings
    WARN  [bg] themingContract.tokens[0].defaultLight: defaultLight not provided
✗ input: 1 error, 0 warnings
    ERROR themingContract.prefix: prefix is required

Validation passed: 3 contracts validated, 2 warnings

docs.title: Usage in Makefiles
docs.text:
Example Makefile for a project using DSS:

DSS ?= dss
WEB_SRC = ./web/src

.PHONY: generate validate package

generate:
    @$(DSS) generate \
        --css $(WEB_SRC)/index.css \
        --types $(WEB_SRC)/lib/design-system-types.ts \
        --llm ./DESIGN_CONTEXT.md

validate:
    @$(DSS) validate $(WEB_SRC)/components

# CI validation with JSON output
validate-ci:
    @$(DSS) validate --json $(WEB_SRC)/components

# Check if generated files are current
check:
    @$(DSS) generate --css /tmp/check.css
    @diff -q $(WEB_SRC)/index.css /tmp/check.css

# Generate NPM package
package:
    @$(DSS) generate --package ./dist --targets all

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
name: Design System Validation

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.22'

      - name: Install dss
        run: go install github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/cmd/dss@latest

      - name: Validate components
        run: dss validate -d ./design-system ./src/components

      - name: Check generated files are current
        run: |
          dss generate -d ./design-system --css /tmp/index.css
          diff ./src/index.css /tmp/index.css

fi

docs.title: Go SDK
docs.text: The Go SDK provides programmatic access to DSS for loading, validating, and generating code from design system specifications.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/sdk/go

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    dss "github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/sdk/go"
)

func main() {
    // Load from directory
    ds, err := dss.LoadDesignSystem("./my-design-system/")
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    // Validate
    if err := ds.Validate(); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    fmt.Printf("Loaded: %s v%s\n", ds.Meta.Name, ds.Meta.Version)
}

docs.text:
ds, err := dss.LoadDesignSystem("./my-design-system/")

The loader scans for:

  • meta.json (required)
  • principles.json, accessibility.json, etc.
  • foundations/, components/, patterns/ subdirectories

docs.title: DesignSystem
docs.text:
type DesignSystem struct {
    Meta          Meta
    Principles    []Principle
    Foundations   Foundations
    Components    []Component
    Patterns      []Pattern
    Templates     []Template
    Content       *Content
    Accessibility *Accessibility
    Governance    *Governance
    ThemeBindings []ThemeBindings  // Application token mappings
}

docs.title: ThemingContract
docs.text:
type ThemingContract struct {
    Prefix      string       // CSS custom property prefix (e.g., "--btn")
    Description string
    Tokens      []ThemeToken
}

type ThemeToken struct {
    ID           string  // Token identifier
    CSSProperty  string  // Full CSS property name
    Semantic     string  // Semantic category for auto-mapping
    Description  string
    DefaultLight string  // Light mode default
    DefaultDark  string  // Dark mode default
}

docs.title: ThemeBindings
docs.text:
type ThemeBindings struct {
    Component string          // Component ID to theme
    SpecURL   string          // Optional URL to fetch component spec
    ThemeMode string          // "light", "dark", or empty for both
    Strategy  string          // "explicit", "semantic", "inherit"
    Mappings  []TokenMapping
}

type TokenMapping struct {
    From      string  // Application token ID
    To        string  // Component token ID
    Transform string  // Optional CSS transform function
}

docs.title: Case Study: Component Theming Contracts
docs.text: How a component library (markdown-editor) and an application (PlexusOne) use DSS to coordinate theming through a formal contract.

docs.title: The Challenge
docs.text:
When integrating third-party components, theming becomes complex:

Challenge Without DSS Discovery Read component source to find CSS variables Mapping Manually map app tokens to component tokens Maintenance No validation when either spec changes Documentation Scattered across READMEs and code comments

docs.title: The Scenario
docs.text:
• markdown-editor: A Lit Web Component with its own design tokens
  • PlexusOne: An application with its own design system
  • Goal: PlexusOne wants to theme markdown-editor using its colors

docs.title: The Solution: Theming Contracts
docs.text:
DSS enables a formal contract between component and consumer:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    COMPONENT (markdown-editor)                       │
│                                                                     │
│   design-system.json                                                │
│   ├── foundations/colors        ← Internal token definitions        │
│   └── themingContract           ← PUBLIC: What consumers can theme  │
│         prefix: "--mde-theme"                                       │
│         tokens: [bg-primary, accent, ...]                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  │ Contract
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    APPLICATION (PlexusOne)                           │
│                                                                     │
│   design-system.json                                                │
│   ├── foundations/colors        ← App token definitions             │
│   └── themeBindings             ← Maps app tokens to components     │
│         @grokify/markdown-editor:                                   │
│           plexus-dark → bg-primary                                  │
│           plexus-cyan → accent                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  │ dss generate
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    GENERATED CSS                                     │
│                                                                     │
│   markdown-editor {                                                 │
│     --mde-theme-bg-primary: var(--plexus-dark);                     │
│     --mde-theme-accent: var(--plexus-cyan);                         │
│   }                                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Schema: Theming Contract (Component Side)
docs.text:
Components declare what can be themed via themingContract:

{
  "meta": {
    "name": "Markdown Editor",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "themingContract": {
    "prefix": "--mde-theme",
    "description": "CSS custom properties for external theming",
    "tokens": [
      {
        "id": "bg-primary",
        "cssProperty": "--mde-theme-bg-primary",
        "semantic": "background",
        "description": "Main background color",
        "defaultLight": "#ffffff",
        "defaultDark": "#0f172a"
      },
      {
        "id": "bg-secondary",
        "cssProperty": "--mde-theme-bg-secondary",
        "semantic": "background",
        "description": "Toolbar and secondary surfaces",
        "defaultLight": "#f8fafc",
        "defaultDark": "#1e293b"
      },
      {
        "id": "accent",
        "cssProperty": "--mde-theme-accent",
        "semantic": "primary",
        "description": "Primary accent for interactive elements",
        "defaultLight": "#3b82f6",
        "defaultDark": "#60a5fa"
      },
      {
        "id": "text-primary",
        "cssProperty": "--mde-theme-text-primary",
        "semantic": "foreground",
        "description": "Primary text color",
        "defaultLight": "#1e293b",
        "defaultDark": "#f1f5f9"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Token Semantics
docs.text:
The semantic field enables automatic mapping:

Semantic Meaning Examples background Surface colors bg-primary, bg-secondary foreground Text colors text-primary, text-muted primary Brand/accent colors accent, link border Edge colors border, divider success Positive states success, valid danger Negative states error, destructive

docs.title: Schema: Theme Bindings (Application Side)
docs.text:
Applications declare how to map their tokens to components:

{
  "meta": {
    "name": "PlexusOne",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "foundations": {
    "colors": [
      { "id": "plexus-dark", "value": "#0a0e1a", "semantic": "background" },
      { "id": "plexus-slate", "value": "#1e293b", "semantic": "background" },
      { "id": "plexus-cyan", "value": "#06b6d4", "semantic": "primary" },
      { "id": "foreground", "value": "#f1f5f9", "semantic": "foreground" }
    ]
  },
  "themeBindings": [
    {
      "component": "@grokify/markdown-editor",
      "specUrl": "https://github.com/grokify/markdown-editor/blob/main/design-system.json",
      "mappings": [
        { "from": "plexus-dark", "to": "bg-primary" },
        { "from": "plexus-slate", "to": "bg-secondary" },
        { "from": "plexus-cyan", "to": "accent" },
        { "from": "foreground", "to": "text-primary" }
      ],
      "themeMode": "dark"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Mapping Strategies
docs.text: Strategy Description When to Use Explicit Manual from/to mapping Full control, custom branding Semantic Auto-match by semantic field Quick integration, standard colors Hybrid Semantic defaults + explicit overrides Balance of automation and control

docs.title: Automatic Semantic Mapping
docs.text:
When semantics align, mappings can be generated automatically:

# Generate bindings by matching semantic fields
dss bind @grokify/markdown-editor --strategy=semantic

The tool:

  1. Fetches component's themingContract
  2. Matches app tokens by semantic field
  3. Generates themeBindings section
  4. Warns about unmatched tokens
✓ Matched: bg-primary ← plexus-dark (semantic: background)
✓ Matched: accent ← plexus-cyan (semantic: primary)
⚠ Unmatched: bg-tertiary (no app token with semantic: background)
  Suggestion: Add mapping or use plexus-slate

  • Published in design-system.json

docs.title: Contract Validation (Component CI)
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/dss.yml
- name: Validate Theming Contract
  run: |
    dss validate design-system.json
    dss contract check --ensure-defaults

Validates:

  • All contract tokens have defaultLight and defaultDark
  • CSS properties follow naming convention
  • Semantics are from allowed set

docs.title: Binding Validation (App CI)
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/dss.yml
- name: Validate Theme Bindings
  run: |
    dss validate design-system.json
    dss bindings check --warn-unbound

Validates:

  • Referenced components exist
  • All to tokens exist in component contract
  • All from tokens exist in app foundations
  • Warns about unmapped contract tokens

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: Benefit Description Discoverability themingContract is the single source of truth for what can be themed Type Safety Schema validation catches mismatches at build time Auto-Generation CSS mappings generated from specs, not hand-written Semantic Matching Tokens with same semantics can auto-bind Documentation Contract is self-documenting, rendered in MkDocs LLM Context AI assistants understand the contract for code generation

Prefix: --mde-theme

docs.title: Future: Theming Contract Registry
docs.text:
A central registry could enable:

# Search for themeable components
$ dss search --has-contract

@grokify/markdown-editor  v1.0.0  Markdown editor with PDF export
@shadcn/ui                v2.0.0  Beautifully designed components

$ dss bind @shadcn/ui --strategy=semantic --output themes/

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
DSS theming contracts formalize the relationship between component libraries and consuming applications:

  1. Components publish what can be themed (themingContract)
  2. Apps declare how to map tokens (themeBindings)
  3. Tools generate CSS from specs (dss generate --bindings)
  4. CI validates contracts don't break (dss bindings check)

This eliminates guesswork, enables automation, and ensures theming stays in sync as both specs evolve.

docs.title: Case Study: PlexusOne Design System
docs.text: How PlexusOne uses DSS to maintain visual consistency across 1 website, 33 MkDocs documentation sites, and Marp presentation decks.

docs.title: The Challenge
docs.text:
PlexusOne is a suite of AI agent tools and libraries spanning multiple products:

  • OmniLLM - Multi-provider LLM abstraction
  • OmniVault - Secrets management for AI agents
  • OmniVoice - Voice AI integration
  • AgentKit - Agent development framework
  • AssistantKit - Assistant UI components
  • Plus 30+ additional libraries and tools

Each product has its own GitHub repository with documentation. Over time, visual inconsistency crept in:

Property Count Problem Main website 1 Custom CSS, no system MkDocs sites 33 Mix of indigo, teal, readthedocs themes Marp presentations ~20 Inconsistent colors, fonts

docs.title: Symptoms of Design Drift
docs.text:
# go-elevenlabs/mkdocs.yml
theme:
  palette:
    primary: indigo
    accent: indigo

# plexusone-apps/mkdocs.yml
theme:
  palette:
    primary: teal
    accent: cyan

# opik-go/mkdocs.yml
theme: readthedocs  # Different theme entirely

The brand was fragmenting. Cyan, purple, and pink were the intended accent colors, but many sites used Material's default indigo. Dark mode was inconsistent. Fonts varied.

docs.title: The Solution: Design System as Code
docs.text: Instead of manually updating 33+ repos, we created a single source of truth using DSS.

docs.title: One Spec, Multiple Outputs
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │            plexusone-specs/design-system/               │
                    │                                                         │
                    │   colors.json  typography.json  spacing.json  ...       │
                    │                                                         │
                    │              THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH                 │
                    └─────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                              │
                              dss generate    │
                                              │
              ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
              │                               │                               │
              ▼                               ▼                               ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐             ┌─────────────────┐             ┌─────────────────┐
    │   web.css       │             │   mkdocs.css    │             │   slides.css    │
    │   Tailwind v4   │             │   MkDocs Mat.   │             │   Marp Theme    │
    └────────┬────────┘             └────────┬────────┘             └────────┬────────┘
             │                               │                               │
             ▼                               ▼                               ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐             ┌─────────────────┐             ┌─────────────────┐
    │                 │             │  33 MkDocs      │             │  ~20 Marp       │
    │    Website      │             │  Documentation  │             │  Presentation   │
    │                 │             │  Sites          │             │  Decks          │
    └─────────────────┘             └─────────────────┘             └─────────────────┘

The key insight: Define design tokens once, generate context-appropriate CSS for each medium. When the brand evolves, update the spec and regenerate—all 54+ properties update together.

plexusone-specs/
└── design-system/
    ├── meta.json              # Brand metadata
    ├── principles.json        # Design philosophy
    ├── foundations/
    │   ├── colors.json        # Cyan/purple/pink palette
    │   ├── typography.json    # Inter + JetBrains Mono
    │   └── spacing.json       # Spacing scale
    ├── contexts/
    │   ├── web.json           # Website-specific adjustments
    │   ├── slides.json        # Brighter colors for projection
    │   └── docs.json          # MkDocs Material config
    └── components/
        ├── button.json
        └── card.json

docs.title: Coverage CI Integration
docs.text:
Add to CI pipeline to prevent coverage regression:

# .github/workflows/design-system.yml
- name: Check DSS Coverage
  run: |
    dss coverage --json -d ./design-system > coverage.json
    SCORE=$(jq '.summary.overallScore' coverage.json)
    if (( $(echo "$SCORE < 90" | bc -l) )); then
      echo "DSS coverage dropped below 90%: $SCORE%"

    fi

docs.title: When DSS Makes Sense
docs.text: DSS is not the right solution for everyone. Here's an honest assessment of when it's worth the investment.

docs.title: Good Fit Criteria
docs.text:
DSS is worthwhile when you have:

Criteria Why It Matters 10+ properties Manual synchronization becomes unsustainable Multiple output formats Same tokens → Tailwind, MkDocs, Marp, etc. AI-assisted development LLMs benefit from structured design context Code-first team Comfortable with JSON, CLI tools, CI/CD Documentation-as-code philosophy Want design decisions versioned and reviewable

PlexusOne checks all five boxes, making DSS a strong fit.

docs.title: When Simpler Alternatives Are Better
docs.text:
Situation Better Alternative Single website CSS custom properties in one file 2-3 MkDocs sites Shared extra.css in a gist or repo No AI development Figma + manual CSS Simple brand (just colors/fonts) Style Dictionary or a 50-line build script Figma-first workflow Figma Tokens plugin → Style Dictionary

The 80/20 rule: A shell script that copies a CSS file to multiple repos solves 80% of the consistency problem with 20% of the effort.

docs.title: Honest Trade-offs
docs.text: Benefit Cost Single source of truth Another system to maintain Comprehensive coverage (98.1%) Significant upfront effort (11 foundation files, patterns, templates, governance, content) LLM-ready context Requires structured JSON authoring Automated validation Learning curve for dss CLI Future-proof May be over-engineering for simple needs

docs.title: Questions to Ask Before Adopting
docs.text:
1. Do you have 10+ properties? If not, manual sync may be fine.
  2. Do you need multiple CSS formats? If everything is React/Tailwind, a shared npm package suffices.
  3. Are AI assistants part of your dev workflow? If not, the LLM context benefit doesn't apply.
  4. Does your team prefer code or visual tools? Figma-first teams may resist JSON-based design specs.
  5. Do you need governance documentation? Small teams communicating directly may not need formal deprecation policies.

docs.title: Why It Worked for PlexusOne
docs.text:
PlexusOne is a tooling company building AI agent infrastructure. The team:

  • Already builds CLI tools and libraries
  • Has 54+ properties across repos
  • Uses AI assistants for code generation
  • Values automation over manual processes
  • Wants design decisions documented alongside code

For this profile, DSS provides clear ROI. For a small team with a single website, it would be over-engineering.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
DSS transformed PlexusOne's fragmented design landscape into a cohesive system. The key insight: treat design as code. Version it, generate outputs for each context, and distribute via packages.

The coverage journey from 29.4% to 98.1% demonstrates that a design system spec is not a one-time effort—it evolves as the system matures. The dss coverage command provides visibility into completeness and helps teams prioritize what to add next.

Bottom line: DSS is worth it if you have the scale (10+ properties), need multiple output formats, and want AI assistants to understand your design system. If you just need shared colors across a few sites, a simple CSS file is the better choice.

Generate complete, publishable NPM packages from your design system specification with framework-specific presets and configurations.

CLI Usage:

# Generate package with all targets
dss generate --package ./dist --targets all

dss generate --package ./dist --targets css,tailwind,shadcn

dss generate --package ./dist --scope @myorg --name tokens

Target Output Use Case css CSS custom properties Vanilla CSS/HTML projects tailwind Tailwind v4 preset and theme Tailwind CSS v4+ projects shadcn ShadCN/UI theme variables ShadCN/UI component library mkdocs-material MkDocs Material theme Documentation sites scss SCSS variables Sass/SCSS projects json Raw JSON tokens Build tool pipelines w3c W3C Design Tokens format Standards-compliant token exchange

dist/
├── package.json           # NPM package manifest with exports
├── index.js               # CommonJS entry point
├── index.mjs              # ES module entry point
├── index.d.ts             # TypeScript declarations
├── README.md              # Usage documentation

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Load design system
cd my-design-system

# Generate NPM package with all targets
dss generate --package ./dist --targets all

# Publish to NPM
cd dist
npm publish

docs.title: SDK Usage
docs.text:
import dss "github.com/plexusone/design-system-spec/sdk/go"

ds, _ := dss.LoadDesignSystem("./my-design-system/")

opts := dss.PackageGeneratorOptions{
    OutputDir:   "./dist",
    Scope:       "@myorg",
    PackageName: "design-tokens",
    Targets: []dss.PackageTarget{
        dss.TargetCSS,
        dss.TargetTailwind,
        dss.TargetShadCN,
    },
}

err := ds.GeneratePackage(opts)

docs.title: Specification Overview
docs.text: DSS defines 9 canonical layers for complete design system specification. Each layer serves a specific purpose and can be defined in separate JSON/YAML files or combined.

docs.title: Layer Summary
docs.text: Layer File(s) Purpose Meta meta.json System name, version, maintainers Principles principles.json Design philosophy and guidelines Foundations foundations/*.json Design tokens (colors, typography, spacing) Components components/*.json UI elements with variants, states, props Patterns patterns/*.json Multi-component solutions Templates templates/*.json Page-level layouts Content content.json Voice & tone guidelines Accessibility accessibility.json WCAG compliance requirements Governance governance.json Versioning and deprecation policies Theming themeBindings.json Token mappings to external components

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
A complete design system spec typically follows this structure:

my-design-system/
├── meta.json                 # Required: name, version
├── principles.json           # Design philosophy
├── accessibility.json        # WCAG requirements
├── governance.json           # Policies
├── content.json              # Voice & tone
├── themeBindings.json        # Token mappings to external components
├── foundations/
│   ├── colors.json           # Color tokens
│   ├── typography.json       # Font definitions
│   ├── spacing.json          # Spacing scale
│   └── border-radius.json    # Border radius values
├── components/
│   ├── button.json           # Button component spec (includes themingContract)
│   ├── card.json             # Card component spec
│   └── input.json            # Input component spec
├── patterns/
│   └── form.json             # Form pattern spec
└── templates/
    └── dashboard.json        # Dashboard template

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
The minimum required spec is just meta.json:

{
  "name": "My Design System",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}

docs.title: Loading Behavior
docs.text:
The DSS loader:

  1. Looks for meta.json in the specified directory
  2. Loads principles.json, accessibility.json, etc. if present
  3. Scans foundations/, components/, patterns/, templates/ subdirectories
  4. Merges all files into a single DesignSystem object
  5. Validates the combined spec

docs.title: File Formats
docs.text:
DSS supports both JSON and YAML:

// colors.json
{
  "colors": [
    { "id": "primary", "value": "#0066CC" }
  ]
}

# colors.yaml
colors:
  - id: primary
    value: "#0066CC"

docs.title: LLM Context
docs.text:
Any component, pattern, or template can include an llm field for AI code generation optimization:

{
  "llm": {
    "intent": "What this element is for",
    "allowedContexts": ["where-to-use-it"],
    "forbiddenContexts": ["where-not-to-use-it"],
    "antiPatterns": ["common mistakes to avoid"],
    "exampleUsage": ["<Component>Example</Component>"]
  }
}

See Components for full LLM context documentation.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Components are the UI building blocks of your design system. Each component spec defines its variants, states, props, and LLM context.

└── components/
    ├── button.json
    ├── card.json
    └── input.json

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
{
  "id": "Button",
  "name": "Button",
  "description": "Interactive button for triggering actions",
  "category": "actions",
  "variants": [...],
  "states": [...],
  "props": [...],
  "slots": [...],

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Unique identifier (used in code generation) name string Human-readable name description string What this component does

docs.title: Optional Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description category string Component category (actions, inputs, layout, etc.) variants array Visual/behavioral variations states array Interactive states (hover, focus, disabled) props array Configurable properties slots array Content insertion points anatomy array Internal structure parts constraints object Size and layout constraints llm object LLM optimization context

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
Variants define the visual or behavioral variations of a component.

{
  "variants": [
    {
      "id": "default",
      "name": "Default",
      "description": "Primary action button",
      "isDefault": true
    },
    {
      "id": "secondary",
      "name": "Secondary",
      "description": "Less prominent actions"
    },
    {
      "id": "destructive",
      "name": "Destructive",
      "description": "Dangerous actions like delete"
    },
    {
      "id": "ghost",
      "name": "Ghost",
      "description": "Minimal button for inline actions"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: States
docs.text:
States define interactive states beyond variants.

{

    {
      "id": "default",
      "name": "Default",
      "description": "Normal resting state"
    },
    {

docs.text:
Props define the configurable properties of a component.

{
  "props": [
    {
      "name": "variant",
      "type": "enum",
      "description": "Visual style variant",
      "required": false
    },
    {
      "name": "size",
      "type": "enum",

      "defaultValue": "default",
      "required": false
    },
    {

    },

      "description": "Render as child element for composition"
    }

}

docs.title: Prop Types
docs.text: Type Description string Text value number Numeric value boolean True/false enum One of predefined values (from variants or sizes) node React node content function Callback function

  }
}

docs.title: Theming
docs.text: DSS provides a formal mechanism for component libraries to publish themeable tokens and for applications to bind their design tokens to those components.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The theming system consists of two complementary schemas:

Schema Used By Purpose themingContract Component libraries Declares which CSS properties can be themed externally themeBindings Applications Maps application tokens to component theming APIs

This separation enables:

  • Components remain agnostic of consuming applications
  • Applications can theme any component that publishes a contract
  • Tools can validate bindings and generate CSS automatically

docs.title: Theming Contract (Component Side)
docs.text:
Components declare their external theming API via themingContract:

{
  "themingContract": {
    "prefix": "--mde-theme",
    "description": "CSS custom properties for external theming",
    "tokens": [
      {
        "id": "bg-primary",
        "cssProperty": "--mde-theme-bg-primary",
        "semantic": "background",
        "description": "Main background color",
        "defaultLight": "#ffffff",
        "defaultDark": "#0f172a"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Contract Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description prefix string Yes CSS custom property prefix (e.g., --mde-theme) description string No Human-readable description of the theming API tokens array Yes List of themeable tokens

docs.title: Token Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string Yes Token identifier (e.g., bg-primary) cssProperty string Yes Full CSS custom property name semantic string Yes Semantic category for automatic mapping description string No What this token controls defaultLight string Yes Default value for light mode defaultDark string Yes Default value for dark mode

docs.title: Semantic Categories
docs.text:
The semantic field enables automatic token matching between component and application:

Semantic Meaning Typical Tokens background Surface colors bg-primary, bg-secondary, bg-tertiary foreground Text colors text-primary, text-secondary, text-muted primary Brand/accent colors accent, link, focus border Edge/divider colors border, divider, outline success Positive states success, valid, complete warning Caution states warning, caution danger Negative states error, destructive, invalid spacing Layout spacing spacing-sm, spacing-md, spacing-lg radius Border radius radius-sm, radius-md, radius-lg typography Font properties font-sans, font-mono, font-size-* elevation Shadows/depth shadow-sm, shadow-md, shadow-lg

docs.title: Implementation Pattern
docs.text:
Components should use the var(--theme-*, default) pattern internally:

:host {
  /* External override takes precedence, falls back to internal default */
  --internal-bg: var(--mde-theme-bg-primary, #ffffff);
}

:host([theme='dark']) {
  --internal-bg: var(--mde-theme-bg-primary, #0f172a);
}

.content {
  background: var(--internal-bg);
}

This pattern ensures:

  • Components work standalone with sensible defaults
  • External theming overrides when properties are set
  • Both light and dark modes are supported

docs.title: Theme Bindings (Application Side)
docs.text:
Applications declare how to map their tokens to component theming APIs:

{
  "themeBindings": [
    {

  2. Matches app tokens by semantic field
  3. Generates themeBindings section
  4. Warns about unmatched tokens

✓ Matched: accent ← plexus-cyan (semantic: primary)
⚠ Unmatched: bg-tertiary (no app token with semantic: background)
  Suggestion: Add mapping or use plexus-slate

docs.title: Web Components and Shadow DOM
docs.text:
This theming system is designed specifically for Web Components:

  • Shadow DOM encapsulation prevents normal CSS from styling internal elements
  • CSS custom properties are the only values that pierce the shadow boundary
  • Theming contracts formalize which properties components expose

Without a contract, consumers must read source code to discover themeable properties. With a contract, the theming API is explicit, documented, and machine-readable.

docs.title: NPM Package Generation Roadmap
docs.text: This document specifies the NPM package generation feature for design-system-spec.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The dss generate --package command generates a complete, publishable NPM package containing design tokens and framework-specific presets from a design system specification.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Currently, design systems like PlexusOne, ProductBuildersHQ, and AIStandardsIO define tokens in JSON specs but must manually create NPM packages for distribution. This feature automates that process, enabling:

  1. Consistent token distribution across projects
  2. Framework-specific presets (Tailwind, ShadCN, MkDocs Material)
  3. TypeScript type safety for token consumers
  4. Version synchronization between spec and published package

docs.text:
# Generate NPM package to ./dist
dss generate --package ./dist

# Generate with specific targets
dss generate --package ./dist --targets tailwind,shadcn,mkdocs-material

# Generate with custom scope
dss generate --package ./dist --scope @myorg

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Design System Specification (DSS) defines a standard, machine-readable format for describing design systems. A DSS document describes:

  • Foundations: Design tokens including colors, typography, spacing, and other primitive values
  • Components: Reusable UI elements with their props, events, slots, and constraints
  • Patterns: Multi-component solutions for common UX scenarios
  • Accessibility: System-wide and component-level a11y requirements
  • LLM Context: Metadata optimized for AI-assisted code generation

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. AI-Native Development: Enable AI agents to generate design-system-compliant code
  2. Code Generation: Support generating CSS, TypeScript types, and documentation
  3. Validation: Enable automated checking of implementations against the spec
  4. Interoperability: Provide a common format for design system tooling

docs.title: DSS Document
docs.text: A document (or set of documents) that defines or describes a design system. A DSS document MUST be a valid JSON or YAML document.

docs.title: Path Templating
docs.text: Not applicable to this specification.

docs.title: Media Types
docs.text: The DSS document SHOULD be served with a media type of application/json or application/yaml.

docs.title: HTTP Status Codes
docs.text: Not applicable to this specification.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The DSS Specification is versioned using a major.minor.patch versioning scheme. The major.minor portion of the version string (e.g., 0.1) SHALL designate the DSS feature set.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
A DSS document is itself a JSON object, which MAY be represented either in JSON or YAML format.

All field names in the specification are case-sensitive.

The schema exposes two types of fields: Fixed fields and Patterned fields.

Fixed fields have a declared name. Patterned fields declare a regex pattern for the field name.

docs.title: Data Types
docs.text:
Primitive data types in the DSS are based on the types supported by JSON:

Type Format Description string A sequence of characters number A numeric value (integer or decimal) integer A whole number boolean true or false array An ordered list of values object A key-value map

docs.title: Rich Text Formatting
docs.text: Throughout the specification description fields are noted as supporting CommonMark markdown formatting.

docs.title: Relative References
docs.text: Not applicable to this specification. All URLs MUST be absolute.

docs.title: Design System Object
docs.text: This is the root object of the DSS document.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description meta Meta Object REQUIRED. Provides metadata about the design system. principles [Principle Object] Design philosophy and brand values. foundations Foundations Object REQUIRED. Design tokens and primitive values. components [Component Object] Reusable UI elements. patterns [Pattern Object] Multi-component UX solutions. templates [Template Object] Page-level layouts. content Content Object Voice, tone, and content guidelines. accessibility Accessibility Object System-wide accessibility requirements. governance Governance Object Versioning and contribution policies.

docs.text:
{
  "meta": {
    "name": "Acme Design System",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "description": "The official design system for Acme products"
  },
  "foundations": {
    "colors": [
      { "id": "primary", "value": "#3b82f6", "usage": "Primary actions" }
    ]
  },
  "components": [
    {
      "id": "button",
      "name": "Button",
      "description": "Interactive button component"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Meta Object
docs.text: Provides metadata about the design system.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description name string REQUIRED. The design system name. version string REQUIRED. The version following semantic versioning. description string A brief overview of the design system. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. maturityLevel integer System maturity level from 1 (experimental) to 5 (stable). repository string URL to the source repository. MUST be a valid URI. documentation string URL to the documentation site. MUST be a valid URI. maintainers [Maintainer Object] People or teams responsible for the system. license string The license identifier (e.g., "MIT", "Apache-2.0").

docs.title: Meta Object Example
docs.text:
{

  "version": "2.1.0",

docs.title: Maintainer Object
docs.text: Represents a person or team responsible for the design system.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description name string REQUIRED. Name of the maintainer or team. email string Email contact. MUST be a valid email format. url string URL to profile or team page. MUST be a valid URI.

docs.title: Foundations Object
docs.text: Contains design tokens and primitive values.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description colors [Color Token Object] Color palette and semantic color tokens. typography Typography Object Font families, sizes, weights, and type scale. spacing Spacing Scale Object Spacing scale for margins, padding, and gaps. elevation [Elevation Token Object] Shadow/depth tokens for layering. motion Motion System Object Animation and transition tokens. grid Grid System Object Layout grid system. breakpoints [Breakpoint Object] Responsive breakpoints. borderRadius [Border Radius Token Object] Corner radius tokens. borderWidth [Border Width Token Object] Border width tokens. opacity [Opacity Token Object] Opacity scale tokens. zIndex [Z-Index Token Object] Z-index layer tokens.

docs.text: Represents a single color in the design system.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier (e.g., "primary-500"). value string REQUIRED. Color value in hex, rgb, rgba, or hsl format. semantic string Color's purpose (primary, secondary, danger, etc.). usage string When and how to use this color. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. contrast Contrast Object Accessibility contrast information. lightModeValue string Alternate value for light mode. darkModeValue string Alternate value for dark mode.

docs.title: Typography Object
docs.text: Defines the type system.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description fontFamilies [Font Family Object] REQUIRED. Available font stacks. fontSizes [Font Size Object] REQUIRED. Font size scale. fontWeights [Font Weight Object] REQUIRED. Available font weights. lineHeights [Line Height Object] REQUIRED. Line height scale. letterSpacings [Letter Spacing Object] Letter spacing scale. typeScale [Type Style Object] Complete type styles.

docs.title: Font Family Object
docs.text: Represents a font stack.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier (e.g., "sans", "serif", "mono"). name string REQUIRED. Display name for the font family. stack string CSS font-family fallback stack. value string Deprecated. Use stack instead. weights [integer] Available font weights (e.g., [400, 500, 700]). source string URL to load the font (e.g., Google Fonts URL). usage string When to use this font family.

docs.title: Spacing Scale Object
docs.text: Defines the spacing system.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description baseUnit string REQUIRED. Fundamental spacing unit (e.g., "4px"). scale [Spacing Token Object] REQUIRED. Spacing tokens.

docs.title: Spacing Token Object
docs.text: Represents a single spacing value.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier (e.g., "xs", "sm", "md"). value string REQUIRED. Spacing value with unit. pixelValue integer Equivalent pixel value for reference.

docs.title: Component Object
docs.text: Represents a reusable UI element.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier (e.g., "button", "modal"). name string REQUIRED. Display name for the component. description string Overview of the component's purpose. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. category string Groups related components (e.g., "inputs", "navigation"). variants [Variant Object] Different visual or behavioral versions. states [State Object] Interactive states (hover, focus, disabled). props [Prop Object] Configurable properties/attributes. events [Component Event Object] CustomEvents emitted by the component. slots [Slot Object] Content insertion points for composition. uses [string] Component IDs that this component depends on. tokensUsed [string] Foundation token IDs used by this component. constraints Constraints Object Usage limitations and requirements. accessibility Component A11y Object Accessibility requirements. llm LLM Context Object AI code generation optimization fields. documentationUrl string URL to detailed documentation. MUST be a valid URI. figmaUrl string URL to Figma component. MUST be a valid URI.

  "id": "button",
  "name": "Button",
  "description": "Interactive button for triggering actions",
  "category": "inputs",
  "props": [
    {
      "name": "variant",
      "type": "string",
      "default": "primary",
      "enumValues": ["primary", "secondary", "destructive"]
    },
    {
      "name": "disabled",
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  ],
  "events": [
    {
      "name": "click",
      "description": "Fired when button is clicked",

    }
  ],
  "llm": {
    "intent": "Trigger user actions",
    "allowedContexts": ["forms", "dialogs", "toolbars"],
    "antiPatterns": ["Multiple primary buttons per view"]

docs.title: Prop Object
docs.text: Represents a configurable property of a component.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description name string REQUIRED. Prop name as used in code. type string REQUIRED. Data type (string, number, boolean, enum, array, object). description string What the prop controls. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. required boolean Whether the prop must be provided. Default: false. default any Default value if not specified. enumValues [string] Allowed values for enum types. constraints Prop Constraints Object Validation rules for the prop value.

docs.title: Prop Constraints Object
docs.text: Defines validation rules for a property value.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description min number Minimum value for number types. max number Maximum value for number types. minLength integer Minimum length for string types. maxLength integer Maximum length for string types. pattern string Regex pattern for string validation. step number Valid increments for number types.

docs.title: Component Event Object
docs.text: Represents a CustomEvent emitted by a component.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description name string REQUIRED. Event name (e.g., "change", "submit"). description string When this event is emitted. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. bubbles boolean Whether event bubbles through DOM. Default: false. composed boolean Whether event crosses shadow DOM boundary. Default: false. cancelable boolean Whether event can be canceled. Default: false. detail [Event Detail Field Object] Schema of the event.detail payload.

docs.title: Event Detail Field Object
docs.text: Describes a field in the event.detail payload.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description name string REQUIRED. Field name in the detail object. type string REQUIRED. Data type of the field. description string What this field contains.

docs.title: Slot Object
docs.text: Represents a content insertion point for composition.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description name string REQUIRED. Slot name. description string What content belongs in this slot. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. required boolean Whether content must be provided. Default: false. allowedComponents [string] Component IDs that can be inserted.

docs.title: Variant Object
docs.text: Represents a visual or behavioral variant of a component.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier for the variant. name string REQUIRED. Display name (e.g., "Primary", "Secondary"). description string When to use this variant. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. isDefault boolean Whether this is the default variant. Default: false. tokenOverrides [Token Override Object] Tokens that differ from base component.

docs.title: State Object
docs.text: Represents an interactive state of a component.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier (hover, focus, disabled, etc.). name string Display name for the state. description string When this state applies. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. tokenOverrides [Token Override Object] Tokens that change in this state.

docs.title: Token Override Object
docs.text: Specifies a token value that differs for a variant or state.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description tokenId string REQUIRED. Token being overridden. value string REQUIRED. Override value.

docs.title: Constraints Object
docs.text: Defines usage limitations for a component.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description minWidth string Minimum recommended width. maxWidth string Maximum recommended width. maxChildren integer Maximum number of child elements. requiredParent string Required parent component ID. forbiddenChildren [string] Components that cannot be nested inside. responsiveBehavior string How the component adapts to viewport changes.

docs.title: LLM Context Object
docs.text: Provides optimization fields for AI code generation.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description intent string Primary purpose of this element. allowedContexts [string] Situations where this element SHOULD be used. forbiddenContexts [string] Situations where this element SHOULD NOT be used. dependencies [string] Other elements this one requires. exampleUsage [string] Code snippets demonstrating correct usage. antiPatterns [string] Common mistakes to avoid. semanticMeaning string User-facing meaning of this element. relatedComponents [string] Commonly used together with. priorityScore integer Preference score (higher = prefer over alternatives).

docs.title: LLM Context Object Example
docs.text:
{
  "intent": "Primary action button for form submissions",
  "allowedContexts": ["form-submit", "modal-confirm", "primary-cta"],
  "forbiddenContexts": ["destructive-action", "navigation"],
  "exampleUsage": [
    "<Button variant=\"primary\">Submit</Button>",
    "<Button variant=\"primary\" disabled={isLoading}>Save</Button>"
  ],
  "antiPatterns": [
    "Don't use for destructive actions like delete",
    "Avoid multiple primary buttons in the same view"
  ]
}

docs.title: Pattern Object
docs.text: Represents a multi-component UX solution.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description id string REQUIRED. Unique identifier. name string REQUIRED. Display name. description string REQUIRED. Purpose and when to use it. CommonMark syntax MAY be used. category string Groups related patterns (e.g., "forms", "navigation"). components [Pattern Component Object] REQUIRED. Components that make up this pattern. layout Pattern Layout Object How components are arranged. behavior string Description of the interaction flow. variations [Pattern Variation Object] Different configurations. accessibility Pattern A11y Object Accessibility requirements. llm LLM Context Object AI code generation fields. documentationUrl string URL to detailed documentation.

docs.title: Pattern Component Object
docs.text: References a component used in a pattern.

docs.title: Fixed Fields
docs.text: Field Name Type Description componentId string REQUIRED. Reference to a component from the components list. role string Component's role in this pattern. required boolean Whether this component is essential. Default: false. quantity string How many instances (e.g., "1", "1+", "0-1"). configuration object Default props for this usage.
